raw:
I remember someone at the laundromat whose basket split, and their wet towels scattered across the floor. Wet towels are so heavy, and then you’ve got nothing to carry them in. I felt bad for them—just looking at that pile and thinking how frustrating it would be when you’re trying to get an ordinary chore done.

I had a spare canvas bag, so I offered it to them. It was something I could actually do, rather than just stand there feeling sorry for them. Canvas is useful that way; you can fold a bag up and hardly think about it until you need it. What stays with me is the towels on the floor, really. It seemed like such a small thing to help with, but I imagined it wouldn’t feel small if you were the person standing there with a broken basket.
